subject: Per-tenant egress lockdown & firewall SLA - runbook + evidence request
body_preview: Initial compliance request for per-tenant egress controls and proof-of-possession for firewall allowlist
messages:
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@greenstonepharma.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.col e@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Rizzo <tom.rizzo@greenstonepharma.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Per-tenant egress lockdown / allowlist evidence request

Hi Marissa,

We're progressing toward an ATO for our private deployment and need clarity on Redwood's per-tenant egress and firewall evidence. Two concrete asks:

1) Can Redwood support per-tenant/static egress IPs for private endpoints (so we can lock on a per-customer allowlist)? If yes — are IPs stable per tenant or per deployment window?

2) For our security review we need an evidence bundle: firewall allowlist sample logs (showing SYN/ACK to allowed destinations), a short runbook that describes the outbound flow for private endpoints, and the controls that prevent cross-tenant egress.

Optional: if static per-tenant IPs are not supported, what recommended mitigations do you offer (e.g., private NAT/proxy, customer-managed egress)?

We'd like the artifact by EOD Thu (2028-03-22) for our internal security gating. If helpful, happy to do a 30m sync.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Patel
Security Engineer — Greenstone Pharma
+aisha.patel@greenstonepharma.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@greenstonepharma.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Per-tenant egress lockdown / allowlist evidence request

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front:

- Yes, we can provide per-tenant static egress IPs for Private deployments hosted in Redwood Private (VPC-backed) when customers opt into our per-tenant NAT allocation option. IPs are stable for the lifetime of the deployment unless the customer requests/re-provisions the connector.

- We'll produce a compact runbook and an evidence bundle including sample firewall logs, NAT allocation manifest, and a signed attestation from our Security team.

Next steps from our side: I'll assemble the runbook + IP list and loop in our Networking and Security SMEs (cc'd below). Can you confirm whether Greenstone needs MTLS termination or just IP-based allowlisting on your perimeter? That affects the sample logs we pull.

I'll aim to get the runbook + IP CSV to you by EOD Thu as requested. If you prefer a quick call, propose Thu 10:00-10:30 PT and I'll send a calendar invite.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@greenstonepharma.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Per-tenant egress lockdown / allowlist evidence request

Team — forwarding Greenstone's asks (see original below). Deliverables and owners I propose:

- David: generate the per-tenant static egress IP manifest for the Greenstone Private deployment and confirm IP stability window + rotation policy. Provide CSV and short explanation of assignment algorithm. (Due Thu EOD)
- Kimberly: produce the runbook (1–2 pages) describing outbound flow from private endpoint -> NAT -> internet, including how KV cache / batch traffic is isolated per tenant and what firewall rules we recommend on the customer perimeter (FQDNs/ports, TLS/SNI guidance). Include a short FAQ on "what breaks if IP reassigns". (Due Thu EOD)
- Ben: confirm whether SLA language or addendum is needed for per-tenant IP guarantees and whether we need an internal sales/CS signoff before we commit.

Links / references: drive doc with template: https://drive.redwoodai.com/Shared/Greenstone/EGRESS-RUNBOOK-V1 and JIRA ticket INF-8421.

Please reply with any blockers. Aisha — I'll share a candidate calendar for Thu 10:00 PT unless you ask for different time.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@greenstonepharma.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 14:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Per-tenant egress lockdown / allowlist evidence request

Hi Aisha — attaching the artifacts we discussed. Summary below and attachments listed at the end.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Per-tenant static egress IPs: supported via our "Per-tenant NAT Allocation" option. Greenstone's deployment has 3 static IPv4s assigned (listed in attachment). These IPs remain stable unless you request a redeploy; we only rotate for infra emergencies and will notify 72h prior.
- Firewall runbook: brief 2-page runbook explaining outbound flow, recommended perimeter ACLs (CIDR, ports 443 outbound only except 53 for DNS when required), FQDN allowlist for optional telemetry endpoints, and guidance for MTLS vs IP-only allowlist.
- Evidence bundle: sample firewall logs showing outbound flows from our egress IPs (sanitized), a manifest CSV (egress-ip-list-20280322.csv), and a zipped artifact with signed attestation (safelist-evidence-greenstone.zip).

Recommended perimeter rules (short):
- Allow TCP port 443 to the 3 IPs in egress-ip-list-20280322.csv
- Deny all other outbound connections from the private endpoint subnet unless explicitly listed
- If you require hostname-level validation, allow: *.redwood-inference.com and telemetry.redwood-inference.com (TLS required)

Temporary mitigations if you prefer not to accept shared static IPs:
- Deploy customer-managed egress NAT and point Redwood Private connector at that NAT (we support private peering to a customer egress hop)
- Or, set up a transparent proxy in your egress path and allowlist only the proxy IP(s)

Attachments: redwood-egress-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook, 2 pages), egress-ip-list-20280322.csv (3 rows: assigned public IPv4s), safelist-evidence-greenstone.zip (sanitized firewall logs + signed attestation from Redwood Security). Also linked: https://drive.redwoodai.com/Shared/Greenstone/EGRESS-RUNBOOK-V1

Next steps:
- Aisha: confirm receipt and whether you need a signed SLA addendum.
- David/Kimberly: please archive the evidence in the customer folder and add IAM audit log snippet to the safelist bundle (INF-8421).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the runbook.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
